title: QLoRA: Efficient Finetuning of Quantized LLMs
authors: T. Dettmers, A. Pagnoni, A. Holtzman, L. Zettlemoyer
before: LoRA made fine-tuning cheap, but the frozen base model still had to fit in memory at 16-bit.
problem: A 65B base model needs hundreds of gigabytes, so the adapters did not help enough.
breakthrough: Quantize the frozen base to 4-bit with a data-type suited to normal weights, and backpropagate through it into the adapters. 65B on one 48GB GPU.
why: It put fine-tuning of large models within reach of individuals, and the resulting models were competitive.
next: The open fine-tuning ecosystem as it exists now.
inherits: Quantized base plus small trainable adapters, the standard cheap fine-tune.
